findings.title: removeStoredCredentialById cannot delete federated recovery-code credentials
findings.body: The lookup was changed to RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(), which now also returns credentials from federated user storage (getFederatedCredentialsStream). However, when all codes are used the code still calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...), which only removes credentials from Keycloak's local storage. For a user whose recovery codes live in a federated user storage, the removal silently does nothing: the 'all codes used' credential persists in the user storage, and every subsequent login will keep re-adding the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action while the stale credential remains. The deletion path needs to handle federated credentials (e.g., via disableCredentialType/updateCredential on the user storage) or skip removal when the credential is federated.

findings.title: Used recovery codes in user storage are never consumed, allowing replay
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential stores the raw generated codes (JSON-serialized plaintext list) in the user storage via UserCredentialModel. Unlike the local keycloak-recovery-authn-codes provider, whose isValid() marks a code as used and persists the updated credential, a federated user storage only validates the presented code against the stored list (see BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid, which does anyMatch without removing anything). Because no updated credential is written back after a successful authentication, a recovery code stored in user storage remains valid forever and can be reused by anyone who has seen it, defeating the one-time-use semantics of recovery codes. Additionally, the codes are transmitted to and held by the user storage as plaintext rather than the hashed form used in local storage, which weakens the at-rest protection for federated stores.
